correctness.rationale: A standalone exact verifier enumerates all 107 nonempty matchings of cube Q3, all 252 Hasse covers and 51 matching pairs; the resulting 5 critical cells (one 0-cell, four 2-cells) and acyclic orientation prove integral homotopy equivalence to a four-sphere wedge. For each of all 48 affine graph automorphisms, the program checks signed boundary equivariance on 4,560 basis incidences and evaluates the exact reduced Lefschetz character. The computed character equals delta plus the exterior-square trace identity in all 48 cases. Finite-group character semisimplicity establishes the rational G-module isomorphism; its four nontrivial N-weights prove vanishing invariants and the rationally acyclic finite quotient by characteristic-zero averaging. No sampled finite data is extrapolated to an infinite family.

originality.rationale: The exact same-object published cube matching result establishes the nonequivariant four-sphere wedge only. New data give all 48 signed homology traces and the natural irreducible splitting into an exterior-square signed-coordinate module and the flip-parity line. Published cube three-cut and octahedral-graph results address different complexes. The Braun-Hough 2016 PDF defines two-row planar grids and makes no cubical representation assertion. Relevant aliases and possible stronger implications were searched; priority remains conditional on sources actually inspected.

An equivalent B3 character may appear in other unpublished or nonindexed equivariant graph-complex literature.

value.rationale: The three-dimensional cube is a canonical vertex- and edge-transitive graph and the first nontrivial three-direction hypercube matching case. The complete four-dimensional rational automorphism module is a structural invariant not fixed by the four-sphere wedge type. Its nontrivial 1+3 irreducible split, exact translation character weights and rationally acyclic full symmetry quotient have precise natural motivations. The fact is complete for one canonical finite object, not an arbitrary parameter selection or a recomputation of ordinary Betti numbers.
